theorems.name: Almgren-Chriss Trajectory Satisfies EL Equation
theorems.description: The closed-form Almgren-Chriss trajectory X(t) = X_0 · sinh(κ(T-t))/sinh(κT) satisfies the Euler-Lagrange equation X''(t) = κ² · X(t) at every t. No condition on sinh(κT) is needed: under Lean's x/0 = 0 the degenerate closed form is the zero path, which satisfies the equation too.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.AlmgrenChriss

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

theorem almgrenChrissPath_satisfies_EL_thm (X_0 κ T t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (deriv (MathFin.almgrenChrissPath X_0 κ T))
      (κ^2 * MathFin.almgrenChrissPath X_0 κ T t) t :=
  MathFin.almgrenChrissPath_satisfies_EL X_0 κ T t

metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof, stated for the trajectory itself: the t-derivative of the first-derivative formula X'(t) = −X_0·κ·cosh(κ(T-t))/sinh(κT) is κ²·X(t) (chain rule on cosh), transported to `deriv` of X by hasDerivAt_deriv_of_eventually (Foundations/DerivOfDeriv.lean), since that formula is X' at every t (hasDerivAt_almgrenChrissPath). Re-export from MathFin. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Market-Making Riccati Coefficient — Closed Form
theorems.description: The scalar Riccati coefficient a(t)=Â·tanh(Â(T−t)) solves a'=a²−Â² (single-asset LQ approximation of multi-asset market making).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.MarketMakingRiccati

/-- **Market-making Riccati coefficient — closed form.** The scalar coefficient
`a(t) = Â · tanh (Â (T − t))` solves the Riccati ODE `a' = a² − Â²`
(Bergault–Evangelista–Guéant–Vieira, single-asset LQ approximation). Re-exports
`MathFin.hasDerivAt_riccatiCoeff`. -/
theorem mm_riccati_closed_form (Â T t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (MathFin.riccatiCoeff Â T) (MathFin.riccatiCoeff Â T t ^ 2 - Â ^ 2) t :=
  MathFin.hasDerivAt_riccatiCoeff Â T t

theorems.name: Market-Making Value Function — Approximate HJ Verification (d=1)
theorems.description: The quadratic ansatz θ̌(t,q)=−A(t)q²−B(t)q−C(t) solves the approximate (quadratic-Hamiltonian) Hamilton–Jacobi equation when (A,B,C) solve the Riccati/linear ODE system.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.MarketMakingRiccati

/-- **Market-making value function — approximate-HJ verification (d = 1).** The quadratic ansatz
`θ̌(t,q) = −A(t) q² − B(t) q − C(t)` has time-derivative equal to the approximate
(quadratic-Hamiltonian) Hamilton–Jacobi right-hand side when `(A, B, C)` solve the scalar
Riccati/linear ODE system. Re-exports `MathFin.valueFunction_satisfies_approxHJ`. -/
theorem mm_value_function_hj
    (γ σ z α₀b α₁b α₂b α₀a α₁a α₂a : ℝ) (hz : 0 < z) (A B C : ℝ → ℝ) (t q : ℝ)
    (hA : HasDerivAt A (2 * z * (α₂b + α₂a) * A t ^ 2 - γ * σ ^ 2 / 2) t)
    (hB : HasDerivAt B (2 * z * (α₁b - α₁a) * A t + 2 * z ^ 2 * (α₂b - α₂a) * A t ^ 2
                        + 2 * z * (α₂b + α₂a) * A t * B t) t)
    (hC : HasDerivAt C (z * (α₀b + α₀a) + z ^ 2 * (α₁b + α₁a) * A t + z * (α₁b - α₁a) * B t
                        + z ^ 3 * (α₂b + α₂a) * A t ^ 2 / 2 + z * (α₂b + α₂a) * B t ^ 2 / 2
                        + z ^ 2 * (α₂b - α₂a) * A t * B t) t) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s => -(A s) * q ^ 2 - B s * q - C s)
      (γ * σ ^ 2 / 2 * q ^ 2 - z * (α₀b + α₀a)
        - α₁b * (2 * A t * q * z + A t * z ^ 2 + B t * z)
        - α₁a * (-2 * A t * q * z + A t * z ^ 2 - B t * z)
        - (1 / (2 * z)) * (α₂b * (2 * A t * q * z + A t * z ^ 2 + B t * z) ^ 2
                    + α₂a * (-2 * A t * q * z + A t * z ^ 2 - B t * z) ^ 2)) t :=
  MathFin.valueFunction_satisfies_approxHJ γ σ z α₀b α₁b α₂b α₀a α₁a α₂a hz A B C t q hA hB hC

theorems.name: Market-Making Closed-Form Quotes — Constant Spread + Linear Skew
theorems.description: The greedy quotes give a constant half-spread A(t)z+c (c=quoteConstA for Model A, quoteConstB for Model B) and an inventory-linear model-independent skew −2A(t)q−B(t).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.MarketMakingRiccati

/-- **Market-making closed-form quotes — constant spread + linear skew (Models A & B).** The greedy
half-spread is constant in inventory (with the model constant `c`: `quoteConstA` for the CARA
Model A, `quoteConstB` for the risk-adjusted Model B), and the skew is inventory-linear and
model-independent (`c` cancels). Re-exports `MathFin.mmHalfSpread_const` / `MathFin.mmSkew_linear`. -/
theorem mm_quotes_spread_skew (A B : ℝ → ℝ) (γ z k t q : ℝ) :
    (MathFin.mmQuoteAsk A B z (MathFin.quoteConstA γ z k) t q
        + MathFin.mmQuoteBid A B z (MathFin.quoteConstA γ z k) t q) / 2
      = A t * z + MathFin.quoteConstA γ z k
    ∧ (MathFin.mmQuoteAsk A B z (MathFin.quoteConstB k) t q
        + MathFin.mmQuoteBid A B z (MathFin.quoteConstB k) t q) / 2
      = A t * z + MathFin.quoteConstB k
    ∧ ∀ c : ℝ, (MathFin.mmQuoteAsk A B z c t q - MathFin.mmQuoteBid A B z c t q) / 2
      = -2 * A t * q - B t :=
  ⟨MathFin.mmHalfSpread_const A B z (MathFin.quoteConstA γ z k) t q,
   MathFin.mmHalfSpread_const A B z (MathFin.quoteConstB k) t q,
   fun c => MathFin.mmSkew_linear A B z c t q⟩

theorems.name: Matrix Riccati Coefficient — Multi-Asset Closed Form
theorems.description: The matrix analogue of the scalar market-making Riccati: the spectral closed form a(t)=U·diag(riccatiCoeff(λᵢ))·Uᴴ solves the matrix Riccati ODE a'=a·a−Â·Â for any Hermitian Â (no matrix tanh required).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.MatrixMarketMakingRiccati

/-- **Matrix Riccati coefficient — multi-asset closed form (BEGV Prop. 2).** For a Hermitian
`Â` with eigendecomposition `Â = U·diag(λ)·Uᴴ`, the spectral closed form
`matrixRiccatiCoeff hÂ T t = U·diag(riccatiCoeff (λᵢ) T t)·Uᴴ` solves the matrix Riccati ODE
`a'(t) = a(t)·a(t) − Â·Â` — no matrix `tanh` required. Re-exports
`MathFin.hasDerivAt_matrixRiccatiCoeff`. -/
theorem mm_matrix_riccati_closed_form {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    {Â : Matrix n n ℝ} (hÂ : Â.IsHermitian) (T t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (MathFin.matrixRiccatiCoeff hÂ T)
      (MathFin.matrixRiccatiCoeff hÂ T t * MathFin.matrixRiccatiCoeff hÂ T t - Â * Â) t :=
  MathFin.hasDerivAt_matrixRiccatiCoeff hÂ T t

metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof re-exported from MathFin/Foundations/MatrixMarketMakingRiccati.lean. Verifies the multi-asset matrix Riccati closed form (spectral reduction: a=U·diag(riccatiCoeff λ)·Uᴴ) solves the matrix ODE a'=a·a−Â·Â for any Hermitian Â, with the matrix-valued derivative taken under the L∞ operator norm. The stochastic optimal-control substrate (true value function, verification theorem) is out of scope, mirroring the single-asset entry. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Matrix Value Coefficient — Multi-Asset Market-Making Riccati
theorems.description: The change of variables A(t)=½·D₊^{-½}·matrixRiccatiCoeff·D₊^{-½} solves the market-making matrix Riccati A'=2·A·D₊·A−(γ/2)·Σ, given a positive diagonal D₊ and Â with Â·Â=γ·(D₊^{½}·Σ·D₊^{½}).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.MatrixMarketMakingRiccati

/-- **Matrix value coefficient — multi-asset market-making Riccati (BEGV Prop. 2, Eq. 11).**
With a positive diagonal `D₊ = diagonal d` and `Â` the Hermitian generator scale
`Â·Â = γ•(D₊^{½}·cov·D₊^{½})`, the change of variables `A(t) = ½•(D₊^{-½}·matrixRiccatiCoeff·D₊^{-½})`
solves the market-making matrix Riccati `A'(t) = 2•(A(t)·D₊·A(t)) − (γ/2)•cov`. Re-exports
`MathFin.hasDerivAt_mmMatrixValueCoeff`. -/
theorem mm_matrix_value_riccati {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (d : n → ℝ) (hd : ∀ i, 0 < d i) (cov : Matrix n n ℝ) (γ : ℝ)
    {Â : Matrix n n ℝ} (hÂ : Â.IsHermitian)
    (hÂsq : Â * Â = γ • (Matrix.diagonal (fun i => Real.sqrt (d i)) * cov
                          * Matrix.diagonal (fun i => Real.sqrt (d i)))) (T t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (MathFin.mmMatrixValueCoeff d hÂ T)
      ((2 : ℝ) • (MathFin.mmMatrixValueCoeff d hÂ T t * Matrix.diagonal d
          * MathFin.mmMatrixValueCoeff d hÂ T t) - (γ / 2) • cov) t :=
  MathFin.hasDerivAt_mmMatrixValueCoeff d hd cov γ hÂ hÂsq T t

Verifies A(t)=½·D₊^{-½}·matrixRiccatiCoeff·D₊^{-½} solves the market-making matrix Riccati A'=2·A·D₊·A−(γ/2)·cov, with D₊=diagonal d positive and Â Hermitian satisfying Â·Â=γ·(D₊^{½}·cov·D₊^{½}) — Â enters by this defining relation (the matrix-square-root construction of Â is out of scope, so the verified content is the change of variables). The optimal-control substrate and the B/C coefficients are out of scope. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Glosten-Milgrom Adverse-Selection Spread Is Positive
theorems.description: The market maker's ask strictly exceeds its bid, from the trader mix alone: a buy moves the posterior on the high value strictly more than a sell does, so the two quotes cannot coincide. The two trade probabilities are derived from the model's four primitives rather than assumed. Requires 0 < theta < 1, which issue #107's acceptance criterion omits. Delivered scope: the quotes ask = E[V | buy] and bid = E[V | sell] are posited by the shape of the conclusion, not derived from a competitive market maker's zero expected profit, which is the content of Glosten-Milgrom (1985); the sell event is the complement of the buy event, so there is no no-trade outcome; one period and two-valued, with no dynamics.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Execution.GlostenMilgrom

open MathFin.Execution MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory

theorem glostenMilgrom_spread_pos_thm {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (H B I : Set Ω)
    (hH : MeasurableSet H) (hB : MeasurableSet B) (hI : MeasurableSet I)
    {θ p VL VH : ℝ}
    (hθ0 : 0 < θ) (hθ1 : θ < 1) (hp0 : 0 < p) (hV : VL < VH)
    (hprior : μ H = ENNReal.ofReal θ)
    (hbuy : B ∩ I = H ∩ I)
    (hindepH : μ (H ∩ I) = ENNReal.ofReal p * ENNReal.ofReal θ)
    (hindepHc : μ (Hᶜ ∩ I) = ENNReal.ofReal p * ENNReal.ofReal (1 - θ))
    (huninfH : 2 * μ ((H ∩ B) \ I) = μ (H \ I))
    (huninfHc : 2 * μ ((Hᶜ ∩ B) \ I) = μ (Hᶜ \ I)) :
    0 < (∫ ω, payoff H VL VH ω ∂(μ[|B])) - (∫ ω, payoff H VL VH ω ∂(μ[|Bᶜ])) :=
  MathFin.Execution.spread_pos_of_model μ H B I hH hB hI hθ0 hθ1 hp0 hV hprior hbuy
    hindepH hindepHc huninfH huninfHc

metadata.reference: Glosten & Milgrom, Bid, ask and transaction prices in a specialist market with heterogeneously informed traders, J. Financial Economics 14 (1985) 71-100
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof from the model's four primitives -- the prior, informed/value independence, informed traders trading on the value, and uninformed traders tossing a coin. Trade probabilities are derived rather than assumed; quotes are Bochner integrals against the conditioned measures; Bayes is applied through ENNReal.toReal with every finiteness side condition discharged. Axioms-clean. LIMITS: one-period and two-valued, with no dynamics -- no sequence of trades and no convergence of quotes to the true value. The competitive market maker's zero-expected-profit condition is NOT formalized: ask = E[V | buy] and bid = E[V | sell] are posited by the shape of the conclusion, not derived. The sell event is modelled as the complement of the buy event, so there is no no-trade outcome. The statement carries 0 < theta < 1, which the acceptance criterion as written omits.
